title: Low degree approximation
statement: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube and a positive integer $k$. Then $\mathbb E(f-f^{\le k})^2\le I(f)/k$. For a real cube function $h$, define $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$ and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation, and $I(h)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}I_i(h)$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function on the n-cube
k is a natural number with 0 < k
replaced:
For $k > 0$, the degree-$k$ truncation approximates $f$ with squared $L^2$ error at
most $I[f]/k$.
